# Stable reduction of curves and stable maps, Part II

## Purpose and conventions

This continuation constructs the moduli stacks of smooth and stable pointed curves from the parent’s stable-family and DVR reduction theory. It develops Hilbert presentations, pointed contraction and expansion, clutching and boundary normalization, coarse projectivity, smooth full-level moduli, Hodge determinants and the integral Noether comparison. Stable compactifications and Torelli maps connect these moduli to arithmetic families and relative Picard parameters. The polynomial nodal-chart calculations supply explicit algebraic inputs to expansion, with their relative and completed-local scope kept precise.

The parent [StableReduction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/tree/3c18d9fbfceed0dc5c1edb1070a3927152d19e28/TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction) owns nodal families, stability, stabilization, stable maps and stable reduction over traits. This continuation starts with the moduli problem and imports those objects. The parent cohomology and duality results retain their locally Noetherian hypotheses. Their extension to arbitrary scheme bases is an explicit supplier obligation.

Write M̄_{g,n} for the groupoid-valued stable moduli stack and M_{g,n} for its smooth-family open. Markings are ordered, disjoint and in the relative smooth locus; g,n≥0 and 2g−2+n>0. Arrows are marking-preserving isomorphisms. Unless a target states a narrower base, family predicates are over arbitrary schemes. A coarse space records classes and does not replace the groupoid or its universal family. The projection of the universal stable curve is proper, flat and nodal; smoothness of its total stack does not make that projection smooth at a node.

Full smooth-curve level requires g≥2 and N≥3 invertible. The homogeneous pairing-similitude problem has a multiplier; choosing ζ_N fixes an exact symplectic component over Z[1/N,ζ_N]. Irreducibility has its own connectedness input. Stable boundary level is constructed by normalization, rather than assumed fine on every nodal family. E=f_*ω denotes the rank-g Hodge bundle and λ=det E its line. The rank-zero determinant is O. Relative Picard points are fppf-sheafified line classes; actual line lifts have an H²_fppf obstruction and, when it vanishes, form a Pic(T)-torsor.

Current [AlgebraicVectorBundles L0B–L0C](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/3c18d9fbfceed0dc5c1edb1070a3927152d19e28/TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicVectorBundles/README.md#l0c--polynomial-operations) owns finite locally free sheaves, duals, symmetric/exterior powers and ordinary determinants with scheme pullback comparisons. Apply these operations on scheme atlases and use the separate stack-descent and ordered exact-sequence contracts. Relative Jacobians, polarizations, degree components, torsors, Picard obstructions and Lie/Hodge comparisons are imported from their exact early JC0/JC1/JC4/JC6 and A0 supplier targets; this roadmap does not reproduce them or consume downstream JC7 to construct fine curve level.

The polynomial chart, its ordinary biduality and positive Ext calculations are explicit algebraic inputs. They do not by themselves prove relative stable reflexivity, identify a pointed completed-local hull, or establish arbitrary completed-coefficient Hom/Ext comparisons. The completed finite-projective tensor limit compares original-ring Hom; the source module need not carry a completed-coefficient action.

<a id="mc-0"></a>
## MC.0 — The pointed curve moduli problem

For every g,n≥0 with 2g−2+n>0 construct the groupoid-valued moduli pseudofunctor of smooth or stable ordered n-pointed genus-g curves over arbitrary schemes, using the parent’s curve-family objects. Establish base-change coherence and effective descent; keep isomorphism groupoids distinct from their sets of isomorphism classes. Construct the universal family with an arbitrary additional section, including sections at a node or coinciding with an existing mark. Export the n canonical marking sections, the proper flat nodal projection and the restriction to the smooth-family base. Smoothness of the total universal stack over Z does not assert smoothness of its projection at a node.

**Layer dependencies:** `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-3-prestable-semistable-stable-and-pointed-curves`, `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.4`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0`, `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.3`.

**Acceptance and remaining obligations:**

- Resolve stable-family/descent types and the locally Noetherian-to-arbitrary-scheme extension; supply the real Lean moduli-pseudofunctor signatures.
- Discharge the owned key sample exports via MC.2 supplier nodes, and express all added API/tests once the geometric types exist. Initial MC.0 source passages have been independently checked; the mathematical owner obligations remain open.
- Supply the actual marking/projection/smooth-restriction geometric Lean types for the four added universal-curve API/test omissions. Native scheme pullback/topology primitives are read and imported; they do not provide effective fppf object descent.

<a id="target-key-moduli-curves"></a>
### Moduli stacks of pointed curves

**Target:** `StableReductionPartII:key/moduli-curves` (definition).

For integers g,n≥0 with 2g−2+n>0, define a single moduli pseudofunctor CurvesModuli(ε,g,n), ε=smooth or stable, on schemes. Its fibre over S is the groupoid of parent curve families f:C→S, proper flat finitely presented of pure relative dimension one, with geometrically connected fibres of arithmetic genus g and an ordered list of n disjoint sections through the relative smooth locus. In the stable flavour fibres are nodal and ω_{C/S}(Σsᵢ) is relatively ample; the smooth flavour is the full subcategory with f smooth. Arrows are marking-preserving S-isomorphisms; pullback is scheme-theoretic base change with its canonical associator. Write M_{g,n} and M̄_{g,n}. This is a groupoid-valued functor; no coarse or fine representability is built into its definition.

**Hypotheses:**

- g,n are nonnegative integers and 2g−2+n>0, with the inequality interpreted in the integers.
- The base S is an arbitrary scheme. The parent supplies the family predicates; its locally Noetherian cohomology and duality theorems require the separate arbitrary-base extension recorded in the gaps.

**Dependencies:** `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-3-prestable-semistable-stable-and-pointed-curves`.

**Construction or proof route:**

1. Use the parent’s stable-pointed and smooth-curve family data, without redefining stability.
2. Form the fibre groupoid using marking-preserving relative isomorphisms.
3. Use pullback universal properties to obtain coherent reindexing; the effective-descent assertion is a separate node.

**Acceptance guards:**

- The genus-zero stable range begins at n=3; a two-pointed rational curve is excluded.
- A self-node contributes two normalization flags to stability.

**Uses:**

- `KEYDEF-algebraicgeometry: algebraicgeometry/moduli-curves, six cited papers`: One shared definition for smooth and stable pointed families, their automorphisms and classifying maps.
- `PAPER-YUAN-26/69 and PAPER-DIMITROV-GAO-HABEGGER-21/10`: Unpointed genus≥2 moduli and full-level universal curves.
- `PAPER-CANNING-LARSON-PAYNE-24/2; PAPER-CHEN-24/1; PAPER-LANDESMAN-LITT-24/9; PAPER-ABDURRAHMAN-VENKATESH-25/54`: Pointed moduli bases for boundary, Hurwitz and versal-family constructions; the consumer-specific constructions remain in their owners.

**API:**

- `CurvesModuli.obj` (data): The fibre groupoid over S has precisely the parent smooth/stable pointed families as objects.
- `CurvesModuli.iso` (characterisation): Morphisms are exactly S-isomorphisms carrying every ordered marking to the marking of the same index.
- `CurvesModuli.pullback` (functoriality): For T→S pull back the family and every section; identity and composition agree via coherent canonical isomorphisms.
- `CurvesModuli.smoothInclusion` (projection): For 2g−2+n>0 the smooth flavour is the full open substack of the stable flavour on families whose structure morphism is smooth; base change identifies this inclusion with the smooth-family locus.
- `CurvesModuli.geometricPoints` (characterisation): Over an algebraically closed field the objects and automorphism groups are those of pointed curves, not only isomorphism classes.
- `CurvesModuli.rationalThreeEquivalence` (equivalence): For every base scheme S, (M₀,₃)_S≅S≅(M̄₀,₃)_S, with unique trivialization of the universal family as (P¹_S;0,1,∞). Supplied by [StableReductionPartII:MC.2/genus-zero-base](#target-mc-2-genus-zero-base).
- `CurvesModuli.crossRatio` (equivalence): Over Spec Z, M₀,₄≅P¹_Z minus {0,1,∞} and M̄₀,₄≅P¹_Z, compatibly with the smooth inclusion and the ordered cross-ratio coordinate. Supplied by [StableReductionPartII:MC.2/cross-ratio](#target-mc-2-cross-ratio).
- `CurvesModuli.stableStackProperties` (structure): For g,n≥0 and 2g−2+n>0, M̄_{g,n} is proper smooth Deligne–Mumford over Spec Z of relative dimension 3g−3+n, and M_{g,n} is its open dense smooth-family locus. Supplied by [StableReductionPartII:MC.2/pointed-dm-theorem](#target-mc-2-pointed-dm-theorem).
- `CurvesModuli.universalForgetful` (compatibility): For 2g−2+n>0, M̄_{g,n+1}≅Z̄_{g,n} over M̄_{g,n}; the universal projection is forgetting the last marking and stabilizing, with its n sections given by expansion when the arbitrary extra section equals an old marking. Supplied by [StableReductionPartII:MC.2/expansion-contraction-inverses](#target-mc-2-expansion-contraction-inverses).
- `CurvesModuli.forgetStabilize` (functoriality): For n≥1 and 2g−2+(n−1)>0, forgetting one marking and applying the parent stabilization gives M̄_{g,n}→M̄_{g,n−1}, canonically compatible with base change, label permutations and repeated forgetting; a rational tail with two markings contracts when one of those markings is forgotten. Supplied by [StableReductionPartII:MC.2/forget](#target-mc-2-forget).

**Unit tests:**

- `CurvesModuli.rationalThree` (computation): Over an algebraically closed field the smooth three-pointed rational curve has a unique isomorphism to (P¹;0,1,∞) and trivial automorphism group.
- `CurvesModuli.rationalTwoExcluded` (non-example): (P¹;0,∞) fails the stable-range condition and has a positive-dimensional automorphism group.
- `CurvesModuli.ellipticInvolution` (non-example): In characteristic zero a pointed elliptic curve (E,0) has the nontrivial automorphism [−1]; its fibre groupoid is not a discrete set.
- `CurvesModuli.selfNodeFlags` (compatibility): An irreducible rational nodal curve with one smooth marking is stable of arithmetic genus one: the normalization has three special flags.
- `CurvesModuli.crossRatioBoundary` (computation): Over an algebraically closed field, M₀,₄ is P¹ minus {0,1,∞}, M̄₀,₄ is P¹, and its three boundary points are the three unordered 2+2 partitions of the four ordered labels. Supplied by [StableReductionPartII:MC.2/cross-ratio](#target-mc-2-cross-ratio).
- `CurvesModuli.stableStackDimensions` (compatibility): The proper smooth Deligne–Mumford stack M̄_{g,n} has relative dimension 3g−3+n in the stable range: dimension zero for (0,3) and one for (0,4) and (1,1); its smooth-family locus is open. Supplied by [StableReductionPartII:MC.2/pointed-dm-theorem](#target-mc-2-pointed-dm-theorem).
- `CurvesModuli.universalRationalFour` (compatibility): (M̄₀,₄)_k→(M̄₀,₃)_k=Spec k is the universal curve P¹_k; its three universal marking sections are the boundary points 0,1,∞, and forgetting the fourth mark contracts the inserted two-marked rational tail there. Supplied by [StableReductionPartII:MC.2/expansion-contraction-inverses](#target-mc-2-expansion-contraction-inverses).
- `CurvesModuli.forgetRationalTail` (degenerate): Attach a rational tail with two distinct markings to a smooth genus-two component at one point. Forget one tail marking: stabilization contracts the tail, carries the retained tail marking to the attachment, and preserves the genus-two component. Supplied by [StableReductionPartII:MC.2/forget](#target-mc-2-forget).

**Sources:**

- [knudsen2](#source-knudsen2), Definitions1.1–1.2,printedpp.162–164 (PDF2–4); groupoid statement p.164. Definition1.1 specifies stable pointed families; Definition1.2 gives cartesian marking-preserving morphisms and states the groupoid-fibred stack property. The log-dualizing ampleness formulation is imported from the parent roadmap.

<a id="target-mc-0-pullback-coherence"></a>
### Pullback coherence for pointed moduli

**Target:** `StableReductionPartII:MC.0/pullback-coherence` (lemma).

The canonical isomorphisms (C×_S T)×_T U≅C×_S U and C×_S S≅C preserve all markings and satisfy the pentagon and unit identities, defining the moduli pseudofunctor on arbitrary schemes.

**Hypotheses:**

- g,n≥0 and 2g−2+n>0; composable morphisms U→T→S of arbitrary schemes.
- Each family and its ordered markings is as in CurvesModuli; preservation of the arbitrary-base family conditions is an explicit open import.

**Dependencies:** [StableReductionPartII:key/moduli-curves](#target-key-moduli-curves), `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Limits.pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Limits.pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso_hom_fst`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Limits.pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso_hom_snd`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.hom_ext`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback_fst_iso_of_right_iso`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-3-prestable-semistable-stable-and-pointed-curves`.

**Construction or proof route:**

1. Use the native scheme pullbacks and pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso with its two projection formulas. For identity base change use the first pullback projection with an identity right leg. Equal projections give equality by pullback.hom_ext, so the pentagon, unit and marking coherence follow by uniqueness.
2. Import the parent’s base-change preservation of geometric genus, nodality, smooth sections and log-dualizing ampleness.

**Acceptance guards:**

- Composition is coherent, not asserted definitionally equal.

**Sources:**

- [knudsen2](#source-knudsen2), Definition1.2,printedp.164 (PDF4),condition(ii). Condition(ii) identifies the source family with the scheme-theoretic pullback. The identity and associativity coherence follow from uniqueness with fixed pullback projections.

<a id="target-mc-0-effective-descent"></a>
### Effective descent of pointed stable curves

**Target:** `StableReductionPartII:MC.0/effective-descent` (theorem).

CurvesModuli(ε,g,n) has effective fppf descent of objects and isomorphisms, hence is a stack; compare with Mathlib’s pseudofunctor IsStack predicate rather than asserting this predicate supplies an algebraic atlas.

**Hypotheses:**

- g,n≥0 and 2g−2+n>0; ε is smooth or stable.
- Use the fppf topology on schemes, retaining marking-preserving isomorphisms and their cocycle.

**Dependencies:** [StableReductionPartII:MC.0/pullback-coherence](#target-mc-0-pullback-coherence), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`, `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.3`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.IsStack`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-2-coherent-curve-theory-duality-and-positivity`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.fppfTopology`.

**Construction or proof route:**

1. Descend the relatively ample log-dualizing line with the family by polarized-scheme descent.
2. Descend the ordered sections and their disjoint smooth-locus condition.
3. Use the parent’s geometric-fibre and base-change characterizations to descend the fixed-genus and stability conditions.

**Acceptance guards:**

- Do not replace the fibre groupoid by isomorphism classes before descent.

**Sources:**

- [knudsen2](#source-knudsen2), Definition 1.2, printed p.164 (PDF4), groupoid-fibred stack assertion. Knudsen calls this a stack and refers to Deligne–Mumford Definition 4.1; the latter paper specializes its general site to the étale topology on p.98. The fppf assertion here is a strengthening using the explicitly requested effective fppf descent of polarized schemes and sections, together with locality of the family conditions; it is not asserted as the printed topology or as a consequence of the IsStack class alone.

<a id="target-mc-0-universal-curve"></a>
### The universal curve with an arbitrary extra section

**Target:** `StableReductionPartII:MC.0/universal-curve` (construction).

Define Z̄_{g,n} over M̄_{g,n} by an object (C/S;s₁,…,sₙ;Δ), where Δ:S→C is an arbitrary additional section. It may hit a node or an old marking. For S→M̄_{g,n} classified by C/S, the fibre product S×_{M̄} Z̄ is canonically C. This representable proper flat nodal morphism is the universal curve; its base change to M_{g,n} is a smooth proper curve, and over M̄_{g,n} its relative smooth locus is the open complement of the fibre nodes.

**Hypotheses:**

- g,n≥0 and 2g−2+n>0; S is an arbitrary scheme and C/S is a stable ordered n-pointed family.

**Dependencies:** [StableReductionPartII:key/moduli-curves](#target-key-moduli-curves), [StableReductionPartII:MC.0/pullback-coherence](#target-mc-0-pullback-coherence), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`.

**Construction or proof route:**

1. The groupoid of pairs (T→S, a section of C_T/T) is the representable fibre category of C.
2. Use its universal property to construct the canonical relative scheme and pullback square.
3. The smooth-universal family is the base change to M_{g,n}; the universal total stack can be smooth over Z even though its projection is nodal.

**Acceptance guards:**

- The universal projection is not a smooth morphism at a node.

**Uses:**

- [StableReductionPartII:MC.2/expansion](#target-mc-2-expansion): Given such C/S with old markings sᵢ and arbitrary extra section Δ, put D=Σsᵢ and J=I_Δ. Let p:J∨⊕O_C(D)→K be the cokernel of the diagonal map h↦(h,h), and put C^s=Proj_C Sym K. Set L_s=K/p(J∨) and L_Δ=K/p(O_C(D)). The canonical invertible quotients sᵢ*K→sᵢ*L_s and Δ*K→Δ*L_Δ give the ordered lifted markings. On the stated locally Noetherian bases the construction commutes canonically with base change and with pointed isomorphisms; the arbitrary-base extension is a recorded gap. On geometric fibres it is an isomorphism at a disjoint smooth new point, inserts a rational tail at a collision, and inserts a rational bridge at a node.
- [StableReductionPartII:MC.3/cotangent-line](#target-mc-3-cotangent-line): For the universal stable pointed curve f:C→M̄_{g,n}, define Lᵢ=sᵢ*ω_{C/M̄}. Each is an invertible sheaf because the marking is in the relative smooth locus; it identifies with sᵢ*Ω¹_{C/M̄}. Base change and relabelling preserve this line. The class ψᵢ=c₁(Lᵢ) is an exported input to the consumer’s tautological Chow-ring construction, not a new Chow theory here.
- [StableReductionPartII:MC.4/finite-projective-cover](#target-mc-4-finite-projective-cover): For g≥2 choose a representable finite surjective morphism V→M̄_g with V a normal integral scheme projective over Z. Pull back the universal stable curve to V. This is a chosen cover with a stable family, not a new fine moduli interpretation of V.
- [StableReductionPartII:MC.5/hodge-bundle](#target-mc-5-hodge-bundle): For the universal stable pointed family f:C→M̄_{g,n}, define E_{g,n}=f_*ω_{C/M̄}. It is locally free of rank g, including rank zero for g=0, and formation commutes with arbitrary base change with its canonical cocycle. The relative dualizing sheaf is untwisted by the markings.

**API:**

- `UniversalCurve.fiber` (universal-property): S×_{M̄} Z̄≅C for every classifying family C/S.
- `UniversalCurve.section` (projection): An S-object of Z̄ over C is an arbitrary section Δ of C/S.
- `UniversalCurve.baseChange` (functoriality): The representing isomorphism is natural in S and respects the pointed-family cocycle.
- `UniversalCurve.marking` (projection): For each ordered marking i, define σ_i:M̄_{g,n}→Z̄_{g,n} by (C/S;s₁,…,sₙ)↦(C/S;s₁,…,sₙ;Δ=s_i). The projection composed with σ_i is the identity; under S×_{M̄}Z̄≅C it is exactly s_i, with coherent arbitrary base change.
- `UniversalCurve.projectionNodal` (structure): The universal projection is representable proper flat finitely presented of pure relative dimension one, with geometrically connected genus-g nodal fibres; for a classifying family C/S its base change is precisely f:C→S. It is smooth at a geometric point exactly when that point of its fibre is smooth.
- `UniversalCurve.smoothRestriction` (compatibility): Base change of Z̄_{g,n} to the full smooth-family substack M_{g,n} is the universal smooth proper n-pointed curve. This differs from taking only the relative smooth locus of Z̄ over all of M̄: a singular stable curve retains its nodal point in the universal fibre.

**Unit tests:**

- `UniversalCurve.nodeAllowed` (degenerate): An extra section at the node of an irreducible one-pointed rational genus-one stable curve is allowed.
- `UniversalCurve.collisionAllowed` (non-example): The extra section may equal s₁; imposing disjointness would give only an open part of the universal curve.
- `UniversalCurve.smoothFiber` (compatibility): Over a smooth curve over an algebraically closed field, the fibre is the whole smooth proper curve.
- `UniversalCurve.nodalProjection` (non-example): Let C/k be an irreducible rational curve with one ordinary node and one smooth marking over an algebraically closed field. Its arithmetic genus is one and it is pointed-stable. The base change of the universal projection to its classifying point is C→Spec k and is not smooth at the node; smoothness of the total universal stack over Z does not make this projection smooth.

**Sources:**

- [knudsen2012](#source-knudsen2012), Introduction,printedpp.1–2,cartesian universal-curve diagram. The Introduction allows an unrestricted extra section, explicitly constructs the cartesian representing square, and identifies the projection as the universal stable pointed curve. The smooth restriction is the base change to the smooth-curve locus.

<a id="mc-1"></a>
## MC.1 — The unpointed Deligne–Mumford construction

For g≥2 construct the tricanonical Hilbert locus with polynomial (6t−1)(g−1), identify its projective-frame torsor and quotient stack, and prove representability, finiteness and unramifiedness of the diagonal. Import the parent’s infinitesimal automorphism vanishing and compute the obstruction space, algebraize versal deformations and obtain independent node-smoothing parameters. Deduce a smooth proper Deligne–Mumford stack over Z of relative dimension 3g−3 with relative normal-crossings boundary. A projective frame is an isomorphism P(f_*ω³)≅P^{5g−6}_S. Its embedded hyperplane line agrees with ω³ up to tensoring by a base invertible sheaf; no linear basis or trivialization of that base line is retained. The canonical relative-polarization locus requires its own relative Hilbert/Isom comparison. Extend locally Noetherian parent cohomology and duality to arbitrary family bases by the separately specified approximation input. The universal Isom scheme is the projective-frame action groupoid U_g×PGL_{5g−5}; its smooth-curve source open is dense. Apply the refined Noetherian scheme criterion to this source before deducing arbitrary-family Isom properness. Stack properness has a separate criterion allowing finite trait extensions. Strict completed local normal-crossings equations require their formal-to-étale comparison.

**Layer dependencies:** `StableReductionPartII:MC.0`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-1-nodes-normalization-and-dual-graphs`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-2-coherent-curve-theory-duality-and-positivity`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-8-canonical-contraction-and-unpointed-stable-reduction`, `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.2`, `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.4`, `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.6`, `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.3`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0`.

**Acceptance and remaining obligations:**

- Finish generic proofs/supplier closure for the DM §4 atlas and stack valuative criteria, which the source explicitly states without proofs. The relevant §1 and §4 statements and §5.1–5.2 application have fresh bounded source receipts; DM §§2–3 and transitive inputs are not wholly re-reviewed.
- Resolve Hilbert/Isom/deformation suppliers and separate each nonroutine formal-to-algebraic criterion.
- Construct the canonical relative-polarization Hilbert locus with its projective-frame/base-line twist and prove its representing property.
- Discharge the coherent Ext/deformation supplier scope and the arbitrary-base extension; source verification of MC.1 alone does not close either obligation.
- Discharge the universal Isom action-groupoid comparison, refined Noetherian source-dense scheme criterion, geometric-fibre infinitesimal criterion and formal-to-étale normal-crossings detection at their exact owner contracts; generic baseline names do not supply those intermediate inputs.

<a id="target-mc-1-tricanonical-cohomology"></a>
### Tricanonical Hilbert polynomial and frame rank

**Target:** `StableReductionPartII:MC.1/tricanonical-cohomology` (application).

Apply the parent’s pluricanonical vanishing, very-ampleness and cohomology/base-change API to a stable genus-g curve, g≥2. Its tricanonical direct image has rank 5g−5, the canonical embedding is into P_S(f_*ω³), of relative projective dimension 5g−6, becoming an embedding into P^{5g−6}_S after a local projective frame, its degree is 6g−6 and its Hilbert polynomial is (6t−1)(g−1). These are the numerical inputs to the Hilbert moduli construction, not a second development of the parent’s curve cohomology.

**Hypotheses:**

- g≥2; every curve family is stable, unpointed, proper, flat and finitely presented with geometrically connected nodal genus-g fibres.
- The base-general conclusion requires the stated foundational and arbitrary-base approximation inputs; parent cohomology/duality results have locally Noetherian base scope.

**Dependencies:** `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.1`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-2-coherent-curve-theory-duality-and-positivity`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-3-prestable-semistable-stable-and-pointed-curves`.

**Construction or proof route:**

1. Use the parent’s m≥2 vanishing and m≥3 very-ampleness, and the requested arbitrary-base extension, to obtain locally free direct images and their compatible evaluation embedding.
2. Compute the degree of ω³ from deg ω=2g−2 and its Hilbert polynomial and rank by the parent’s Riemann–Roch.

**Acceptance guards:**

- For m=3 the rank is 5g−5 and the projective dimension is 5g−6.

**Sources:**

- [dm](#source-dm), Theorem 1.2 and its corollary, printed pp.77–78 (PDF4–5). Theorem 1.2 proves vanishing for m≥2 and very ampleness for m≥3 on geometric stable curves. Its corollary and following displayed polynomial give the rank and Hilbert numbers; arbitrary-base extension of the parent theorem is explicitly open.

<a id="target-mc-1-obstruction-vanishing"></a>
### Vanishing of stable-curve obstruction space

**Target:** `StableReductionPartII:MC.1/obstruction-vanishing` (theorem).

For a proper geometrically connected nodal curve C over an algebraically closed field k, Ext²_{O_C}(Ω¹_{C/k},O_C)=0. The local-to-global map Ext¹_{O_C}(Ω¹_{C/k},O_C)→⊕_{x a node} Ext¹_{O_{C,x}}(Ω¹_{C/k,x},O_{C,x}) is surjective.

**Hypotheses:**

- C/k is proper, geometrically connected, nodal and pure one-dimensional; k is algebraically closed.
- Ext is coherent-sheaf Ext on C; its local terms use the stalk of Ω¹_{C/k}.

**Dependencies:** `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.6`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-1-nodes-normalization-and-dual-graphs`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-2-coherent-curve-theory-duality-and-positivity`.

**Construction or proof route:**

1. Use the lci nodal two-term resolution and local Ext sheaves supported at finitely many nodes.
2. Apply the local-to-global Ext spectral sequence and H²=0 on curves; H¹ of a finite-support sheaf vanishes.

**Acceptance guards:**

- Obstructions vanish, while one independent smoothing parameter remains per node.

**Sources:**

- [dm](#source-dm), Lemma 1.3 p.79 (PDF6), and Proposition 1.5 with proof pp.81–82 (PDF8–9). Lemma 1.3 proves Ext² vanishing for a one-dimensional generically smooth lci scheme using the local-to-global spectral sequence. Proposition 1.5 proves surjectivity onto the finite set of local singularity deformation spaces. Proper nodal curves meet these hypotheses; the generic coherent Ext package is still a supplier obligation.

<a id="target-mc-1-tricanonical-hilbert"></a>
### The tricanonical Hilbert locus

**Target:** `StableReductionPartII:MC.1/tricanonical-hilbert` (construction).

For g≥2 put r=5g−5 and E=f_*ω_{C/S}³. Define U_g as the locally closed Hilbert subscheme of P^{r−1}_Z representing isomorphism classes of stable genus-g families C/S equipped with an S-isomorphism α:P_S(E)≅P^{r−1}_S. The embedded curve is obtained by composing the complete tricanonical embedding C→P_S(E) with α. It has Hilbert polynomial (6t−1)(g−1). On an embedded family, O_C(1) identifies with ω_{C/S}³ up to tensoring by the pullback of an invertible sheaf from S; no trivialization of that base line is part of the projective-frame data. Impose the canonical relative polarization and complete-projective-frame condition, not just the Hilbert polynomial.

**Hypotheses:**

- g≥2 and r=5g−5; projective bundles parametrize rank-one quotients of E.
- S is an arbitrary scheme; the extension of the parent locally Noetherian direct-image/base-change theory remains an explicit gap.

**Dependencies:** [StableReductionPartII:MC.1/tricanonical-cohomology](#target-mc-1-tricanonical-cohomology), `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.2`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-3-prestable-semistable-stable-and-pointed-curves`, `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.3`.

**Construction or proof route:**

1. Use the parent tricanonical evaluation embedding C→P_S(f_*ω³) and the fixed-polynomial universal flat Hilbert family.
2. Construct the stable locally closed Hilbert locus with the complete canonical relative polarization. Compare O_C(1)⊗ω^{-3} with a base line, retaining that line in descent; a projective frame need not lift to a linear frame.
3. Use relative Hilbert/Isom representability and the projective-frame functor to identify U_g; changing α defines the PGL_r action. The required relative-polarization and projective-bundle comparison inputs are requested explicitly.

**Acceptance guards:**

- A curve with the same Hilbert polynomial but the wrong polarization is excluded.

**Uses:**

- [StableReductionPartII:MC.1/frame-torsor](#target-mc-1-frame-torsor): For a stable genus-g family C/S, g≥2, the fibre product S×_{M̄_g} U_g is the PGL(5g−5)-torsor of projective frames of P(f_*ω³); it is representable smooth and surjective over S.
- [StableReductionPartII:MC.4/finite-degree-equations](#target-mc-4-finite-degree-equations): Let S be a noetherian scheme and f:X→S a stable genus-g family with g≥2. On each quasi-compact finite-type parameter family, choose a common sufficiently large d such that Symᵈ(f_*ω³)→f_*ω^{3d} is surjective and its degree-d kernel determines every tricanonically embedded geometric fibre. For the moduli application S is a proper finite-type scheme cover of the coarse moduli space over Z; the same relative Serre argument applies over Z and over a field. The bound may depend on the family, and d=2 is not assumed.

**API:**

- `TricanonicalHilbert.universal` (data): Pull back the universal embedded stable curve with its complete tricanonical projective frame; O_C(1)≅ω³⊗f*L for an invertible sheaf L on the base, without a chosen trivialization of L.
- `TricanonicalHilbert.frame` (characterisation): S-points of U_g identify with stable C/S equipped with α:P_S(f_*ω³)≅P^{5g−6}_S, modulo pointed-family isomorphisms carrying α to α; no linear frame or base-line trivialization is retained.
- `TricanonicalHilbert.action` (structure): PGL(5g−5) acts by changing the projective frame and preserves the locus.

**Unit tests:**

- `TricanonicalHilbert.genusTwo` (computation): For g=2 the embedding is in P⁴, has degree6, and Hilbert polynomial6t−1.
- `TricanonicalHilbert.wrongPolarization` (non-example): The Hilbert polynomial alone does not impose the complete tricanonical relative polarization: the additional condition is O_C(1)≅ω³⊗f*L for a base line L, together with the complete projective-frame comparison.
- `TricanonicalHilbert.pullback` (compatibility): A base change of a framed family corresponds to the base change of its point of U_g.
- `TricanonicalHilbert.projectiveFrameTwist` (non-example): Over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic zero fix a smooth genus-g curve C₀ with a tricanonical projective coordinate, g≥2, and put r=5g−5. Let S=D_+(det)⊂P(Mat_r)=P^{r²−1}_k, so S≅PGL_{r,k}. The constant family C₀×S with its tautological varying projective coordinate is an S-point of U_g. Its embedded hyperplane line is pr_C₀*ω_{C₀/k}³⊗pr_S*O_S(1); O_S(1) has exact order r in Pic(S), so it is nontrivial. Requiring an untwisted global hyperplane identification would exclude this projectively framed family.

**Sources:**

- [dm](#source-dm), Printed p.78 (PDF5), displayed isomorphism of the H_g functor; Proposition 5.1 proof p.104 (PDF31). The displayed functor parametrizes isomorphisms of projective bundles, not bases of the direct image. Its universal embedding therefore retains the scalar-lift base-line twist. Proposition 5.1 identifies the atlas fibre with the projective-bundle Isom scheme. The twist test is an explicit deduction using the central GL_r→PGL_r quotient, not a printed example.
- [stacks-projective-bundles-review](#source-stacks-projective-bundles-review), Definition27.21.1 and rank-one quotient representing property. The quotient convention identifies the tricanonical evaluation embedding and its pulled-back hyperplane line. The varying-matrix example uses homogeneous coordinates bilinear in the curve coordinate and the projective matrix.
- [stacks-projective-picard-review](#source-stacks-projective-picard-review), Lemma31.29.5, complete statement and proof. Projective matrix space has Picard group Z generated by O(1). For the varying-frame test, remove the irreducible determinant divisor of degree r; the explicit divisor argument in the review then gives Pic(PGL_r)=Z/r. Apply the lemma only in positive dimension n=r²−1≥24; its missing n≥1 hypothesis is recorded as E14.
- [stacks-picard-extension-review](#source-stacks-picard-extension-review), Lemma31.29.3, complete statement and proof. Invertible sheaves on the determinant complement extend to projective matrix space. The kernel consists of line bundles supported on that single determinant divisor, giving the quotient by rZ in the review counterexample.

<a id="target-mc-1-isom-representable"></a>
### Representability of the Isom functor

**Target:** `StableReductionPartII:MC.1/isom-representable` (theorem).

For two stable genus-g families g≥2 over S, Isom_S(C,D) is represented by a quasi-projective S-scheme of finite presentation, compatible with arbitrary base change; a marked Isom functor is its closed subfunctor imposing equality of each ordered section.

**Hypotheses:**

- g≥2; every curve family is stable, unpointed, proper, flat and finitely presented with geometrically connected nodal genus-g fibres.
- The base-general conclusion requires the stated foundational and arbitrary-base approximation inputs; parent cohomology/duality results have locally Noetherian base scope.

**Dependencies:** [StableReductionPartII:MC.1/tricanonical-cohomology](#target-mc-1-tricanonical-cohomology), `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.2`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0`.

**Construction or proof route:**

1. Apply polarized relative Isom representability to the canonical polarization.
2. For markings use the closed equalizers of their evaluations on the separated target family.

**Acceptance guards:**

- The representing object is not the set of geometric isomorphism classes.

**Sources:**

- [dm](#source-dm), Definition 1.10 and following paragraph, printed p.84 (PDF11). The source invokes polarized Hilbert-related representability for Isom of stable unpointed families. The additional ordered-marking equalizers are an explicit separated-target deduction, retaining finite-presentation and base-change supplier hypotheses.

<a id="target-mc-1-versal-node-parameters"></a>
### Independent node-smoothing parameters

**Target:** `StableReductionPartII:MC.1/versal-node-parameters` (theorem).

For a geometric stable genus-g curve g≥2 with r nodes, a versal deformation over the complete unramified coefficient ring has formally smooth base with 3g−3 variables and local node equations uv=tᵢ for r distinct parameters; the framed base has an additional dim PGL(5g−5) smooth factor. The parameters are chart-local and may be permuted by stabilizers.

**Hypotheses:**

- k is algebraically closed; C/k is stable, unpointed and of genus g≥2, with r nodes.
- The coefficient ring is k in characteristic zero and the complete unramified Cohen ring with residue k in characteristic p; node branches are split over k.
- Use a deformation with a fixed identification of its special fibre with C; stabilizers still act on this chart.

**Dependencies:** [StableReductionPartII:MC.1/obstruction-vanishing](#target-mc-1-obstruction-vanishing), [StableReductionPartII:MC.1/tricanonical-cohomology](#target-mc-1-tricanonical-cohomology), `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.6`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-3-prestable-semistable-stable-and-pointed-curves`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-2-coherent-curve-theory-duality-and-positivity`.

**Construction or proof route:**

1. The local node deformation has one smoothing coordinate per node.
2. Surjectivity of the global-to-local tangent map and obstruction vanishing give a smooth lifting map.
3. Use curve Riemann–Roch and duality on the normalization: with total component genus G, v components and r nodes, the branches contribute 2r marked points, and the tangent spaces preserving them have total dimension 3G−3v+2r. Adding r independent local smoothing parameters and g=G+r−v+1 gives 3g−3. Algebraize the deformation with its ample ω³ and use the projective-frame torsor for the additional PGL_r smooth factor, where the frame rank is 5g−5.

**Acceptance guards:**

- An automorphism can permute node parameters; no globally chosen ordering of nodes is asserted.

**Sources:**

- [dm](#source-dm), Proposition 1.5 pp.81–82 (PDF8–9), following universal formal deformation and framed comparison pp.82–83; Theorem 1.6 p.83 (PDF10). The global-to-local deformation morphism is formally smooth; each split node has one uv=t parameter. The following algebraization and frame comparison give the local Hilbert chart. The dimension 3g−3 uses the listed curve Riemann–Roch and infinitesimal-automorphism inputs.

### The projective-frame torsor

**Target:** `StableReductionPartII:MC.1/frame-torsor` (theorem).

For a stable genus-g family C/S, g≥2, the fibre product S×_{M̄_g} U_g is the PGL(5g−5)-torsor of projective frames of P(f_*ω³); it is representable smooth and surjective over S.

**Hypotheses:**

- g≥2; C/S is a stable unpointed genus-g family over a scheme S; projective frames trivialize P_S(f_*ω³).

**Dependencies:** [StableReductionPartII:MC.1/tricanonical-hilbert](#target-mc-1-tricanonical-hilbert), `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.4`, [StableReductionPartII:key/moduli-curves](#target-key-moduli-curves), [StableReductionPartII:MC.0/effective-descent](#target-mc-0-effective-descent).

**Construction or proof route:**

1. Use the framed representing property and locally free base change.
2. Trivialize f_*ω³ locally; transitions are projective linear maps.
3. Import the smoothness of PGL over Z and descent of a torsor.

**Acceptance guards:**

- The torsor need not have a global section.

**Sources:**

- [dm](#source-dm), Proposition5.1 proof,p.104. The proof identifies H_g×_{M̄_g}S with projective-bundle isomorphisms, a smooth surjective PGL_{5g−5}-torsor. Trivializing the vector bundle gives local sections; projective frame changes define the action.

<a id="target-mc-1-isom-unramified"></a>
### Unramified Isom scheme

**Target:** `StableReductionPartII:MC.1/isom-unramified` (theorem).

The stable-curve Isom scheme is unramified over its base, including in positive characteristic; its geometric tangent spaces at automorphisms vanish.

**Hypotheses:**

- g≥2; every curve family is stable, unpointed, proper, flat and finitely presented with geometrically connected nodal genus-g fibres.
- The base-general conclusion requires the stated foundational and arbitrary-base approximation inputs; parent cohomology/duality results have locally Noetherian base scope.

**Construction or proof route:**

1. At a geometric isomorphism identify its tangent vectors with H⁰(C,T_C); import the parent’s vanishing for stable geometric curves in every characteristic.
2. Use the requested finite-presentation geometric-fibre infinitesimal criterion to obtain uniqueness of all square-zero affine lifts, then apply the native FormallyUnramified.of_hom_ext criterion. That native theorem alone does not turn one field-valued tangent calculation into the family statement.

**Acceptance guards:**

- No characteristic-zero assumption is used.

**Sources:**

### Hilbert quotient presentation

**Target:** `StableReductionPartII:MC.1/hilbert-quotient` (theorem).

For g≥2 the natural morphism [U_g/PGL(5g−5)]→M̄_g is an equivalence of stacks; it gives a finite-type smooth atlas and does not require a GIT coarse quotient.

**Hypotheses:**

- g≥2; every curve family is stable, unpointed, proper, flat and finitely presented with geometrically connected nodal genus-g fibres.
- The base-general conclusion requires the stated foundational and arbitrary-base approximation inputs; parent cohomology/duality results have locally Noetherian base scope.

<a id="target-mc-1-isom-proper"></a>
### Properness of stable-curve Isom

**Target:** `StableReductionPartII:MC.1/isom-proper` (theorem).

The stable-curve Isom scheme is proper over the base. For a trait any generic-fibre isomorphism between stable models extends uniquely; do not require the generic fibre to be smooth in the final theorem.

**Hypotheses:**

- g≥2; every curve family is stable, unpointed, proper, flat and finitely presented with geometrically connected nodal genus-g fibres.
- The base-general conclusion requires the stated foundational and arbitrary-base approximation inputs; parent cohomology/duality results have locally Noetherian base scope.

**Dependencies:** [StableReductionPartII:MC.1/isom-representable](#target-mc-1-isom-representable), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-8-canonical-contraction-and-unpointed-stable-reduction`, [StableReductionPartII:MC.1/versal-node-parameters](#target-mc-1-versal-node-parameters), [StableReductionPartII:MC.1/frame-torsor](#target-mc-1-frame-torsor), [StableReductionPartII:MC.1/hilbert-quotient](#target-mc-1-hilbert-quotient).

**Construction or proof route:**

1. Reduce locally on S to the universal pair of Hilbert families over U_g×U_g using tricanonical projective frames. Under the framed representing property, the scheme of isomorphisms between that universal pair is U_g×PGL_r, r=5g−5: an isomorphism φ:C₁→C₂ induces P(E₁)→P(E₂), and its unique frame change is α₂ P(φ) α₁⁻¹; conversely a frame change gives the corresponding embedded isomorphism. This is the action-groupoid description, not just a statement about orbit classes or the density of U_g×U_g.
2. The source open consisting of smooth curves is U_g^sm×PGL_r. Independent versal node-smoothing parameters make U_g^sm dense; the smooth projection U_g×PGL_r→U_g is open and surjective, so this inverse image is dense. The source is of finite type over the Noetherian scheme U_g×U_g.
3. Apply the refined Noetherian scheme criterion of Stacks tag 0208: it suffices to extend maps from generic points of irreducible components of the universal Isom source over DVRs. Those generic points lie in the displayed smooth-curve open. The parent unpointed smooth-generic stable-model uniqueness gives the unique extension. This does not apply a field-extension existence criterion for stacks to a scheme.
4. Pull back this proper universal Isom scheme to arbitrary pairs of stable families after their local projective frames; properness is local on the target and stable under base change. The family/cohomology approximation input remains explicit. Its valuative consequence then supplies extension for every valuation ring and for nodal generic fibres as well; no such general uniqueness is assumed in the smooth-generic test.

**Acceptance guards:**

- The final Isom theorem includes singular generic stable curves.
- The universal Isom scheme is the action groupoid U_g×PGL_r, whose smooth-curve open is dense. Density of the ambient pair space alone cannot justify testing only smooth-generic isomorphisms.

**Sources:**

- [dm](#source-dm), Theorem 1.11 proof p.84 (PDF11), Lemma 1.12 pp.84–85 (PDF11–12). Theorem 1.11 first reduces to the universal Hilbert pair and asserts source density of its smooth-curve Isom open, then applies smooth-generic DVR uniqueness. The action-groupoid identification U_g×PGL_r and the open smooth projection supply that density here. The a posteriori paragraph removes smooth-generic and DVR restrictions only after the properness theorem.
- [stacks-noetherian-valuative-KKjBS6](#source-stacks-noetherian-valuative-KKjBS6), Tag 0208, Lemma 32.15.3(4) and proof of (4)⇒(1). This scheme theorem justifies the generic-point DVR refinement over a locally Noetherian target. Its proof uses a proper birational Chow cover and a DVR dominating the local ring of a missing projective-boundary point. It is an owner request, not a baseline theorem or a fresh proof of the generic inputs.

For g≥2, M̄_g→Spec Z is smooth of relative dimension 3g−3, and M_g is its dense open substack of smooth curves.

### Relative normal-crossings boundary

**Target:** `StableReductionPartII:MC.1/normal-crossing-boundary` (theorem).

For g≥2 the boundary Δ=M̄_g minus M_g is an effective Cartier divisor with relative normal crossings over Z: on an étale local regular chart its equation is a unit times ∏_{i=1}^r tᵢ. Its global irreducible components need not be smooth and the divisor need not have simple normal crossings.

**Hypotheses:**

- g≥2; every curve family is stable, unpointed, proper, flat and finitely presented with geometrically connected nodal genus-g fibres.
- The base-general conclusion requires the stated foundational and arbitrary-base approximation inputs; parent cohomology/duality results have locally Noetherian base scope.

<a id="target-mc-1-proper-moduli"></a>
### Properness from stable reduction

**Target:** `StableReductionPartII:MC.1/proper-moduli` (theorem).

For g≥2 M̄_g→Spec Z is proper as a morphism of algebraic stacks. The existence test permits a finite extension of the trait fraction field; the separatedness test uses unique isomorphism extension.

**Hypotheses:**

- g≥2; every curve family is stable, unpointed, proper, flat and finitely presented with geometrically connected nodal genus-g fibres.
- The base-general conclusion requires the stated foundational and arbitrary-base approximation inputs; parent cohomology/duality results have locally Noetherian base scope.

**Dependencies:** [StableReductionPartII:MC.1/finite-unramified-diagonal](#target-mc-1-finite-unramified-diagonal), `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.4`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-8-canonical-contraction-and-unpointed-stable-reduction`, [StableReductionPartII:MC.1/smooth-dimension](#target-mc-1-smooth-dimension).

1. Use smooth-dimension to identify the dense open smooth-curve substack M_g of the separated finite-type stack M̄_g.
2. Apply the dense-open reduction in Deligne–Mumford criterion 4.19: it suffices to test smooth generic curves over complete DVRs with algebraically closed residue field.

- A family can require a finite ramified extension to acquire a stable model.

## MC.2 — Universal curves and the full pointed stable range

Identify the universal stable curve over M̄_{g,n} with M̄_{g,n+1} by contraction and expansion, including old-mark collisions and nodal bridges, with natural inverse comparisons and arbitrary-base-change coherence. Establish the genus-zero base(0,3), the genus-one base(1,1), the proper smooth Deligne–Mumford theorem of relative dimension3g−3+n for every stable pair, M₀,₄ and its compactification. The labelled genus-one triangle locus imposes four smoothing parameters: its three internal nodes and the attachment; a nodal genus-one component has a fifth. Universal-curve induction also adds old-section collision divisors to the inverse image of the old boundary.

For the explicit polynomial nodal chart over any commutative coefficient ring, including the zero ring, use the monic ordered coordinates to plan matrix exactness, signed cokernel presentations of the actual section ideal J and dual D=Hom_R(J,R), the denominator-free dual generator, residue and scalar correction, coefficient flatness and arbitrary coefficient base change. Specify the native tensor algebra, its action on the tensor dual, the R′-linear comparison and actual residue quotient, with identity/composition laws. The section evaluation projection is A-linear; it is not generally R-linear. The ideal is finitely presented over its node ring without noetherianity. For flat ambient R→B compare the extended ideal, dual and multiplication quotient; reflection needs faithful flatness. For noetherian R, compare their one-ring adic completions with the corresponding actual completed-ring objects.

Tensor the alternating matrix complexes with every A-module M without assuming M flat, using A-flat presentation cokernels. Plan their tensor cokernel equivalences, ordinary R-biduality, both canonical arbitrary-coefficient Hom exchanges and coefficient naturality. Use the actual augmented finite-free R-projective resolutions, signed categorical Hom-cochain comparisons and both native Mathlib positive Ext interfaces to obtain Ext_R^{n+1}(J,R⊗_A M)=Ext_R^{n+1}(D,R⊗_A M)=0. The canonical second exchange identifies the bidual composite with the first Hom exchange; over noetherian A these polynomial calculations meet the relative stable-reflexivity criterion. Its reusable owner-level predicate/theorem is a separate input.

For compatible coefficient/chart ideals p,m construct Â→R̂ and its scalar tower. Keep R̂⊗_A N→R̂⊗_Â N as the explicitly surjective balancing quotient, without unjustified injectivity. With p finitely generated identify finite-quotient tensor diagrams and their native limits. Transport the completed coefficient action to the original-base limit. For finite free and then finite projective Â-modules N, assemble the ordinary tensor R̂⊗_Â N as the native limit, with retraction-independent projections and inverse laws; no arbitrary-N or general finitely presented interchange is asserted. For any R-module L, including J,D without a completed action, compare Hom_R(L,R̂⊗_Â N) with compatible finite-quotient Hom_R families when N is finite projective over Â. This is not completed-ring Hom or higher Ext.

The reusable relative stable-reflexivity/two-base completion theorem for arbitrary completed coefficients, Knudsen Appendix Proposition6 Bourbaki input and Proposition7 exercise, faithful reflection, pointed completed-local hull, formal-Proj flatness transfer, coherent family/sheaf descent and arbitrary-base approximation remain explicit owner gaps. The polynomial model does not substitute for those geometric inputs. All geometric stages remain partial.

A labelled setup applies only to the statement or hypothesis that links to it. Every formula and finiteness condition below is retained from that target; subsequent local hypotheses can specialize its range. In particular finite-projective hypotheses in a setup govern its assembly/equivalence assertions, rather than every projection constructed before those hypotheses.

<a id="target-mc-2-binary-node-form"></a>
### The binary quadratic node form

**Target:** `StableReductionPartII:MC.2/binary-node-form` (definition).

For a commutative ring A and γ,δ∈A define q_{γ,δ}(x,y)=x²+γxy+δy². Its nondegeneracy condition is that γ²−4δ is a unit. Over a field this describes a possibly nonsplit ordinary double point, including characteristic two. The definition is the polynomial form; the discriminant condition is an explicit hypothesis, not an arbitrary predicate field.

**Hypotheses:**

- The full range, base and auxiliary data are specified in the statement; none are suppressed by a global stable-pair convention.

**Dependencies:** `mathlib:CommRing`, `mathlib:RingHom`, `mathlib:IsUnit`.

**Construction or proof route:**

1. Construct the polynomial and its evaluation using the existing ring operations.
2. Use the determinant of its derivative coefficient matrix for the discriminant; the lifting lemma is a separate node.

**Acceptance guards:**

- No division by2 is used.

**Uses:**

- [StableReductionPartII:MC.2/small-extension-coordinate-correction](#target-mc-2-small-extension-coordinate-correction): Let A be a commutative ring, ε²=0, and d=γ²−4δ a unit. Every zero-constant-term series f=d(xu+yv) admits μ=−2δu+γv and ν=γu−2v such that q(x+εμ,y+εν)=q(x,y)+εf. The identity works also in characteristic two.
- [StableReductionPartII:MC.2/pointed-node-normal-form](#target-mc-2-pointed-node-normal-form): Let Λ be complete noetherian local with residue field k and let q over k have unit discriminant. The pointed node k[[x,y]]/(q), with x,y↦0, has a formally versal hull A_pd=Λ[[s,t]] and R_pd=A_pd[[x,y]]/(q̃(x,y)−q̃(s,t)), with section x↦s,y↦t. The tangent map is an isomorphism k²→k². This is a hull, not a claim that the deformation groupoid is represented by a fine scheme.
- [StableReductionPartII:MC.2/node-matrix-factorization](#target-mc-2-node-matrix-factorization): For a commutative ring A and γ,δ,x,y,s,t∈A define Φ=((δy+δt+γx,x+s+γt);(−(x−s),y−t)) and Ψ=((y−t,−(x+s+γt));(x−s,δy+δt+γx)). These explicit matrices constitute the special node-section factorization; their polynomial product relation and the noetherian nodal exactness theorem are separate nodes. No unit-discriminant hypothesis is needed to form the matrices.
- [StableReductionPartII:MC.2/node-factorization-products](#target-mc-2-node-factorization-products): For a commutative ring A and arbitrary γ,δ,x,y,s,t∈A, the displayed Φ and Ψ satisfy ΦΨ=ΨΦ=(q(x,y)−q(s,t))I₂. This polynomial identity needs neither noetherianity nor the unit-discriminant hypothesis.
- [StableReductionPartII:MC.2/node-factorization-exact](#target-mc-2-node-factorization-exact): Set q=X²+γXY+δY², F=q(X,Y)−q(s,t), R=A[Y][X]/(F), u=[X], v=[Y], ι:A→R, c=u−ιs, d=v−ιt, b=u+ιs+ιγ·ιt, a=ιδ·v+ιδ·ιt+ιγ·u, J=(c,d), D=Hom_R(J,R). In this actual quotient the alternating Φ,Ψ complex and its transpose are exact: ker Φ=im Ψ, ker Ψ=im Φ, ker Φᵀ=im Ψᵀ and ker Ψᵀ=im Φᵀ. Cokernel identifications are the two separate construction nodes.

**API:**

- `NodeForm.eval` (simp): q(x,y)=x²+γxy+δy².
- `NodeForm.map` (functoriality): For a ring map φ, φ(q(x,y))=q_{φγ,φδ}(φx,φy).
- `NodeForm.linearCorrection` (relation): For ε²=0 and f=(γ²−4δ)(xu+yv), the explicit coordinate changes μ=−2δu+γv and ν=γu−2v give q(x+εμ,y+εν)=q(x,y)+εf. This ring identity specializes to formal power series; expressing a zero-constant series as xu+yv is the separate algebraic input.

**Unit tests:**

- `NodeForm.split` (computation): q_{0,−1}(x,y)=x²−y²; this is nondegenerate when2 is invertible.
- `NodeForm.characteristicTwo` (computation): Over a characteristic-two field q_{1,0}=x²+xy has unit discriminant1 and two distinct branches.
- `NodeForm.doubleLineExcluded` (non-example): q_{0,0}=x² has discriminant0 and is excluded from the nondegenerate node hypothesis.

**Sources:**

- [knudsen2012](#source-knudsen2012), Definition1.1,pp.4–5. The cited passage supplies the construction or proof in the stated range; qualifications and upstream inputs are explicit in the statement and prerequisites.

<a id="target-mc-2-forget"></a>
### Forgetting a marking on the moduli stack

**Target:** `StableReductionPartII:MC.2/forget` (construction).

For 2g−2+n>0 define the morphism π:M̄_{g,n+1}→M̄_{g,n} by the parent’s single-mark contraction after forgetting the last mark. The contraction sends the removed mark to an arbitrary section of the contracted curve, hence lifts π to a morphism c:M̄_{g,n+1}→Z̄_{g,n}. Repeated forgetting is coherent and respects permutations of retained labels.

**Hypotheses:**

- g,n are nonnegative integers in the explicitly stated stable range 2g−2+n>0; family bases are schemes.
- Parent contraction/cohomology inputs have locally Noetherian scope until the separate approximation gap is discharged.

**Dependencies:** [StableReductionPartII:key/moduli-curves](#target-key-moduli-curves), [StableReductionPartII:MC.0/pullback-coherence](#target-mc-0-pullback-coherence), `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-3-prestable-semistable-stable-and-pointed-curves`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-9-marked-stabilization-and-stable-pointed-reduction`.

**Construction or proof route:**

1. Apply the already-owned family contraction on every fibre category.
2. Use its uniqueness and base-change cocycle to descend a stack morphism; record the image of the removed section.

**Acceptance guards:**

- Forgetting into the unstable range is not part of the morphism.

**Uses:**

- [StableReductionPartII:MC.2/expansion-contraction-inverses](#target-mc-2-expansion-contraction-inverses): The expansion morphism s:Z̄_{g,n}→M̄_{g,n+1} and contraction morphism c are quasi-inverse equivalences over M̄_{g,n}. Their unit and counit are natural pointed-family isomorphisms; consequently M̄_{g,n+1} is the universal curve of M̄_{g,n}.
- [StableReductionPartII:MC.3/forget-cotangent-line](#target-mc-3-forget-cotangent-line): For π:M̄_{g,n+1}→M̄_{g,n} and retained i, let D_{i,n+1} be the divisor of a rational tail carrying exactly marks i,n+1 and its attachment. Then Lᵢ on the source is π*Lᵢ⊗O(D_{i,n+1}); equivalently π*Lᵢ=Lᵢ⊗O(−D_{i,n+1}).
- [StableReductionPartII:MC.5/hodge-forgetting](#target-mc-5-hodge-forgetting): For π:M̄_{g,n+1}→M̄_{g,n}, π*E_{g,n}≅E_{g,n+1} and therefore π*λ_{g,n}≅λ_{g,n+1}, canonically with coherent repeated forgetting.

**API:**

- `ForgetMarking.map` (projection): The target family is the parent forget-last contraction.
- `ForgetMarking.extraSection` (data): The removed section descends to an arbitrary section of the contracted family.
- `ForgetMarking.compose` (functoriality): Different coherent orders of forgetting the same set give canonically isomorphic morphisms.

**Unit tests:**

- `ForgetMarking.rationalTail` (degenerate): Forgetting one of two markings on a rational tail contracts that tail and carries the remaining mark to its attachment.
- `ForgetMarking.rationalBridge` (degenerate): Forgetting the sole marking on a rational bridge replaces that bridge by a node.
- `ForgetMarking.unstableTargetExcluded` (non-example): The putative map M̄₀,₃→M̄₀,₂ is excluded by the stated target range.

**Sources:**

- [knudsen2](#source-knudsen2), Proposition 2.1, printed p.174 (PDF14), including its final stack-morphism paragraph. The proposition constructs a unique contraction for stable (n+1)-pointed curves with stable target (g,n), and explicitly describes c:M̄_{g,n+1}→Z̄_{g,n}. Repeated-forgetting coherence is imported from the parent; it is not proved by Corollary 2.6 alone.

### The three-pointed rational moduli scheme

**Target:** `StableReductionPartII:MC.2/genus-zero-base` (theorem).

M₀,₃=M̄₀,₃≅Spec Z. Every ordered smooth three-pointed rational family is uniquely trivialized as (P¹;0,1,∞); no singular stable genus-zero three-pointed fibre exists.

**Hypotheses:**

- The fixed stable pair is (g,n)=(0,3); S is a base scheme.

**Dependencies:** [StableReductionPartII:MC.0/effective-descent](#target-mc-0-effective-descent), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-1-nodes-normalization-and-dual-graphs`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-3-prestable-semistable-stable-and-pointed-curves`.

**Construction or proof route:**

1. Use the normalization genus and stable-flag count to exclude reducible stable three-pointed trees.
2. Trivialize the genus-zero family locally and use the unique three-point projectivity; descend the unique trivialization.

**Acceptance guards:**

- The automorphism group of the ordered triple is trivial.

**Sources:**

- [knudsen2](#source-knudsen2), Theorem 2.7 proof, printed p.179 (PDF19), initial g=0,n=3 case. The induction starts with M̄₀,₃=Spec Z. The exact three-pointed family trivialization and exclusion of singular trees are supplied by the parent graph/stability data and effective descent; this is the exported base case.

<a id="target-mc-2-small-extension-coordinate-correction"></a>
### Coordinate correction over a small extension

**Target:** `StableReductionPartII:MC.2/small-extension-coordinate-correction` (theorem).

Let A be a commutative ring, ε²=0, and d=γ²−4δ a unit. Every zero-constant-term series f=d(xu+yv) admits μ=−2δu+γv and ν=γu−2v such that q(x+εμ,y+εν)=q(x,y)+εf. The identity works also in characteristic two.

**Hypotheses:**

- The full range, base and auxiliary data are specified in the statement; none are suppressed by a global stable-pair convention.

**Dependencies:** [StableReductionPartII:MC.2/binary-node-form](#target-mc-2-binary-node-form).

**Construction or proof route:**

1. Expand the two squares and the cross term.
2. Terms with ε² vanish; the remaining coefficient is d(xu+yv).

**Acceptance guards:**

- Whenγ=1 and char2 the formulas still give the required correction.

**Sources:**

<a id="target-mc-2-node-matrix-factorization"></a>
### The node-section matrix factorization

**Target:** `StableReductionPartII:MC.2/node-matrix-factorization` (construction).

For a commutative ring A and γ,δ,x,y,s,t∈A define Φ=((δy+δt+γx,x+s+γt);(−(x−s),y−t)) and Ψ=((y−t,−(x+s+γt));(x−s,δy+δt+γx)). These explicit matrices constitute the special node-section factorization; their polynomial product relation and the noetherian nodal exactness theorem are separate nodes. No unit-discriminant hypothesis is needed to form the matrices.

**Hypotheses:**

- The full range, base and auxiliary data are specified in the statement; none are suppressed by a global stable-pair convention.

**Dependencies:** [StableReductionPartII:MC.2/binary-node-form](#target-mc-2-binary-node-form), `mathlib:Matrix`, `mathlib:Matrix.of`, `mathlib:Matrix.scalar`.

**Construction or proof route:**

1. Use the pinned Matrix.of to form the two matrices from their four entries.
2. The product relation and exactness are separate applications; forming the two matrices does not depend on those proofs.

**Acceptance guards:**

- The general Eisenbud regular-local MCM equivalence is not needed.

**Uses:**

- [StableReductionPartII:MC.2/node-factorization-products](#target-mc-2-node-factorization-products): For a commutative ring A and arbitrary γ,δ,x,y,s,t∈A, the displayed Φ and Ψ satisfy ΦΨ=ΨΦ=(q(x,y)−q(s,t))I₂. This polynomial identity needs neither noetherianity nor the unit-discriminant hypothesis.
- [StableReductionPartII:MC.2/node-factorization-exact](#target-mc-2-node-factorization-exact): Set q=X²+γXY+δY², F=q(X,Y)−q(s,t), R=A[Y][X]/(F), u=[X], v=[Y], ι:A→R, c=u−ιs, d=v−ιt, b=u+ιs+ιγ·ιt, a=ιδ·v+ιδ·ιt+ιγ·u, J=(c,d), D=Hom_R(J,R). In this actual quotient the alternating Φ,Ψ complex and its transpose are exact: ker Φ=im Ψ, ker Ψ=im Φ, ker Φᵀ=im Ψᵀ and ker Ψᵀ=im Φᵀ. Cokernel identifications are the two separate construction nodes.

**API:**

- `NodeSectionFactorization.left` (projection): The left matrix is Φ with the stated entries.
- `NodeSectionFactorization.right` (projection): The right matrix is Ψ with the stated entries.
- `NodeSectionFactorization.products` (relation): ΦΨ=ΨΦ=(q(x,y)−q(s,t))I₂.
- `NodeSectionFactorization.PolynomialModel.cokernels` (characterisation): In the polynomial quotient, cokernel Ψ is J via [z]↦cz₀−dz₁; cokernel Φ is Hom_R(J,R) via [z]↦z₀incl−z₁ε. These are separate construction nodes.

**Unit tests:**

- `NodeSectionFactorization.characteristicTwo` (compatibility): The same product identities hold when2=0 andγ=1.
- `NodeSectionFactorization.repeatedRootExcluded` (non-example): The geometric node conclusions require unit discriminant; the raw matrix product identity alone does not exclude a double line.
- `NodeSectionFactorization.PolynomialModel.receivingRingNotExact` (non-example): Unit discriminant with both matrices zero in Z gives kernel Z² and image zero; the actual polynomial quotient is essential.

**Sources:**

<a id="target-mc-2-section-hom-differential"></a>
### The polynomial section Hom differential

**Target:** `StableReductionPartII:MC.2/section-hom-differential` (construction).

For any commutative ring A and γ,δ,s,t∈A, use the actual polynomial ring R=A[Y][X]/(X²+γXY+δY²−(s²+γst+δt²)), its coefficient map ι:A→R, u=[X], v=[Y], c=u−ιs, d=v−ιt, b=u+ιs+ιγ·ιt and a=ιδ·v+ιδ·ιt+ιγ·u. For any A-module M put N=R⊗_A M with its native left R-action and H=Hom_R(R²,N). Write L_W(h)=h∘W for native R-linear precomposition and E:R²⊗_A M≃Hom_R(R²,N) for the previously specified finite-free tensor coordinates. Define d(e,n):H→H for e∈{false,true} and n≥0: choose L_Φ if (n mod 2=0) has the same truth value as e=true, and L_Ψ otherwise. The false phase is the section-ideal Hom sequence; the true phase is the dual Hom sequence.

**Suggested declaration:** `NodeSectionFactorization.PolynomialModel.sectionHomDifferential`.

**Hypotheses:**

- A is any commutative ring and M is any A-module; no flatness of M, noetherianity, nontriviality or unit-discriminant hypothesis is imposed for this polynomial calculation.

**Acceptance guards:**

- Do not infer Ext vanishing, relative stable reflexivity, completed-local comparisons or family/sheaf descent from this cochain result alone.

**Uses:**

- `Knudsen2012 §3 and StableReductionPartII:MC.2/dual-section-ideal`: Retain the two actual alternating resolutions in Hom coordinates, as the next input to native projective-resolution and Ext comparison.
- `The native coefficient-module Hom comparison nodes in MC.2`: Fix the actual degree-zero phase and the signed augmentation, keeping degree-zero Hom distinct from positive-degree vanishing.

**API:**

- `NodeSectionFactorization.PolynomialModel.sectionHomDifferential_ideal_zero` (compatibility): The actual degree-zero differential d(false,0) equals L_Ψ, as required by ker(P_J)=im(Ψ).
- `NodeSectionFactorization.PolynomialModel.sectionHomDifferential_dual_zero` (compatibility): The actual degree-zero differential d(true,0) equals L_Φ, as required by ker(P_D)=im(Φ).
- `NodeSectionFactorization.PolynomialModel.sectionHomDifferential_periodic` (relation): For either phase e and every n≥0, d(e,n+2)=d(e,n) as an R-linear map.
- `NodeSectionFactorization.PolynomialModel.sectionHomDifferential_exact` (characterisation): For either phase e and every n≥0, d(e,n) then d(e,n+1) form an exact pair.
- `NodeSectionFactorization.PolynomialModel.sectionHomDifferential_sq` (relation): For either phase e and every n≥0, d(e,n+1)∘d(e,n)=0 as an actual R-linear map H→H.

**Unit tests:**

- `NodeSectionFactorization.PolynomialModel.sectionHomDifferential.test_ideal_signed_column` (computation): With γ=δ=s=t=0, every A and every m∈M, d(false,0)(E((0,1)⊗m))(1,0)=u⊗m; this fixes the Ψ starting phase.
- `NodeSectionFactorization.PolynomialModel.sectionHomDifferential.test_dual_negative_column` (computation): With γ=δ=s=t=0, every A and every m∈M, d(true,0)(E((0,1)⊗m))(1,0)=−u⊗m; this fixes the Φ starting phase and its negative entry.

<a id="target-mc-2-pointed-node-normal-form"></a>
### Normal form of a pointed nodal deformation

**Target:** `StableReductionPartII:MC.2/pointed-node-normal-form` (theorem).

Let Λ be complete noetherian local with residue field k and let q over k have unit discriminant. The pointed node k[[x,y]]/(q), with x,y↦0, has a formally versal hull A_pd=Λ[[s,t]] and R_pd=A_pd[[x,y]]/(q̃(x,y)−q̃(s,t)), with section x↦s,y↦t. The tangent map is an isomorphism k²→k². This is a hull, not a claim that the deformation groupoid is represented by a fine scheme.

**Hypotheses:**

- The full range, base and auxiliary data are specified in the statement; none are suppressed by a global stable-pair convention.

**Dependencies:** [StableReductionPartII:MC.2/binary-node-form](#target-mc-2-binary-node-form), [StableReductionPartII:MC.2/small-extension-coordinate-correction](#target-mc-2-small-extension-coordinate-correction), `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.6`.

**Construction or proof route:**

1. Use power-series division by a monic quadratic to express each element uniquely as f(y)+xg(y); flatness of noetherian formal power-series rings gives flatness of R_pd.
2. Lift pointed coordinates across a small extension and use coordinate correction to remove the error.
3. Use flatness and nilpotent Nakayama to show that the resulting surjective map has zero kernel.
4. Compute the tangent pair from the images of x,y under the section.

**Acceptance guards:**

- Do not assert absence of automorphisms in the pointed-node deformation groupoid.

**Sources:**

- [knudsen2012](#source-knudsen2012), Proposition2.1 and Lemmas2.5,2.7–2.9,pp.6–10. The cited passage supplies the construction or proof in the stated range; qualifications and upstream inputs are explicit in the statement and prerequisites.

### Kernel of section evaluation

**Target:** `StableReductionPartII:MC.2/section-evaluation-kernel` (lemma).

Set q=X²+γXY+δY², F=q(X,Y)−q(s,t), R=A[Y][X]/(F), u=[X], v=[Y], ι:A→R, c=u−ιs, d=v−ιt, b=u+ιs+ιγ·ιt, a=ιδ·v+ιδ·ιt+ιγ·u, J=(c,d), D=Hom_R(J,R). ev∘ι=id_A, ker(ev)=J, and 0→J→R→A→0 splits A-linearly by ι.

**Hypotheses:**

- A is any commutative ring, including the zero ring; γ,δ,s,t∈A. No noetherianity, regularity of A or unit discriminant is assumed for this polynomial-model statement.

**Dependencies:** [StableReductionPartII:MC.2/polynomial-node-model](#target-mc-2-polynomial-node-model), `mathlib:Polynomial.mem_span_C_X_sub_C_X_sub_C_iff_eval_eval_eq_zero`, `mathlib:Polynomial.eval₂_evalRingHom`, `mathlib:AdjoinRoot.induction_on`, `mathlib:AdjoinRoot.lift_mk`, `mathlib:Ideal.map_span`, `mathlib:Ideal.mem_map_of_mem`, `mathlib:Ideal.span_le`.

**Construction or proof route:**

1. Use the built AdjoinRoot.induction_on to represent r by a bivariate polynomial P. The built lift_mk and eval₂_evalRingHom identify section evaluation with (P.eval(C s)).eval t.
2. The built Polynomial.mem_span_C_X_sub_C_X_sub_C_iff_eval_eval_eq_zero puts every vanishing representative in span{C(Y−t),X−C(s)}. This already proves the two-variable division statement; do not plan a private generic remainder lemma.
3. Map that ideal through the actual AdjoinRoot.mk using Ideal.mem_map_of_mem and Ideal.map_span. Its two generator images are v−ιt and u−ιs, so the image lies in J.
4. Conversely both generators evaluate to zero. Ideal.span_le puts J in the actual evaluation kernel. AdjoinRoot.lift_of and evaluation on constants give ev∘ι=id_A.
5. The A-linear splitting is made explicit by the separate section-evaluation-split construction. This proof does not use a normal-form basis, noetherianity, a unit discriminant or flatness of a coefficient map.

**Acceptance guards:**

- The splitting is A-linear; the section map ι is not R-linear for the evaluation action on A.

**Sources:**

- [knudsen2012](#source-knudsen2012), §3, printed pp.11–12: monic division, κ/λ comparisons and proof of Proposition3.1. The explicit polynomial model and its maps are read directly here. 3. For j∈J, ev(j)=0 makes p(j)=j. For a∈A, ev(ι(a))=a makes p(ι(a))=0.
4. Use these two identities in both inverse laws of sectionSplit and as the actual coefficient-flatness retraction.

- Use the existing polynomial quotient, coefficient algebra and actual ideal carrier; no new scalar action, chosen basis or unit discriminant.
