<a id="mc-7"></a>
## MC.7 — Level Picard parameters and consumer interfaces

For a fixed genus g≥2, level N≥3 invertible and degree d∈Z define the level-Picard parameter functor and compare it with relative Picᵈ of the universal smooth curve. Keep the fppf-sheafified Picard functor distinct from globally existing line bundles; identify triples only over algebraically closed fields or under the explicit Brauer-obstruction vanishing condition. Export the moduli and family interfaces to the six key-definition consumers, without rebuilding their Hurwitz stacks, mapping-class groups or tautological Chow rings. Import degree components, representability and torsors from JC0 and the exact JC4 obstruction under universal global functions. Lifts form a Pic(T)-torsor; base twists and dual-number tangent deformations discriminate the definition. Consumer exports retain their exact genus/base/stack ranges, and Chen’s pointed coarse M_{1,1} scheme is supplied by the existing all-stable-pairs coarse-space node.

**Layer dependencies:** `StableReductionPartII:MC.0`, `StableReductionPartII:MC.6`, `JacobianChallengePartII:JC0`, `JacobianChallengePartII:JC4`, `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:A0-extension`.

**Acceptance and remaining obligations:**

- Finish transitive JC0 degree-component/representability/torsor and JC4 cohomological obstruction supplier proofs and their actual types; verify universal global functions on arbitrary test bases. The exact supplier statements are now imported, not missing owner plans.
- Supply actual sheaf/groupoid Lean signatures, including Pic(T)-torsors of lifts and infinitesimal points. The six consumer contracts have fresh bounded source/export receipts; their global composition and routed Yuan/DGH closure remain unverified.

<a id="target-mc-7-level-picard-parameter"></a>
### The degree-d level Picard parameter functor

**Target:** `StableReductionPartII:MC.7/level-picard-parameter` (definition).

For g≥2, N≥3 invertible with a fixed ζ_N pairing component, and d∈Z, define P_g,N^d=Pic^d_{C_g/M_g[N]} on the fppf site. This represented smooth quasi-projective degree-d sheaf is a torsor under the relative Jacobian, parametrizing sheafified relative line classes on the universal smooth curve. An algebraically closed field point corresponds to an isomorphism class of triples (C,α,L). For a general T→M_g[N], lifting a sheaf point to an actual degree-d line bundle is controlled by the boundary to H²_fppf(T,G_m); when it vanishes, the line-bundle isomorphism classes lifting that point form a torsor under Pic(T) by base pullback. The triple groupoid and this sheaf are distinct.

**Hypotheses:**

- g≥2, N≥3 invertible and d an arbitrary integer; the fixed pairing component is over Z[1/N,ζ_N].
- The universal curve lies over the Noetherian fine scheme and is smooth projective with geometrically connected genus-g fibres, so JC0 representability and torsor statements apply. For every test base T, use O_T≅(f_T)_*O_{C_T} universally from the specified parent stable-family/cohomology contract before applying the exact obstruction and kernel statements.

**Dependencies:** [StableReductionPartII:MC.4/fine-level-scheme](#target-mc-4-fine-level-scheme), `JacobianChallengePartII:JC0/relative-degree-components`, `JacobianChallengePartII:JC0/picard-representability`, `JacobianChallengePartII:JC0/picard-torsors`, `JacobianChallengePartII:JC4/actual-to-relative-obstruction`, `JacobianChallengePartII:JC6/picard-lie-cohomology`, `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:A0-extension/relative-picard-base-change`, `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:A0-extension/section-picard-split`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-3-prestable-semistable-stable-and-pointed-curves`, [StableReductionPartII:MC.4/level-rigidity](#target-mc-4-level-rigidity).

**Construction or proof route:**

1. Apply JC0/relative-degree-components, JC0/picard-representability and JC0/picard-torsors to the universal curve on its Noetherian fine base. Representability and all arbitrary-base-change identifications use the imported A0-extension Picard sheaf, not global representatives.
2. Verify the universal global-functions isomorphism for the proper flat smooth geometrically connected family, then apply JC4/actual-to-relative-obstruction to every pullback C_T/T. Its exact sequence is 0→Pic(T)→Pic(C_T)→Pic_{C_T/T}(T)→H²_fppf(T,G_m)→H²_fppf(C_T,G_m). Restrict the lifting assertion to the degree-d component.
3. Exactness gives existence when the boundary vanishes and the Pic(T)-torsor of lifts, using injectivity of base pullback. A chosen curve section kills the boundary and permits the A0-extension/section-picard-split rigidification; no section of the unpointed universal curve is assumed.
4. Over algebraically closed k, choose an fppf-local actual line representative. A nonempty finite-type open of the covering scheme has a k-point, whose pullback supplies an actual line on C_k; thus the boundary of every relative point vanishes. Pic(k)=0 makes the lift class unique. Full-level rigidity controls the curve-level isomorphism; scalar line automorphisms survive in the groupoid.
5. Use JC6/picard-lie-cohomology on a constant smooth genus-two family over C for the dual-number test, together with the exact arbitrary-pullback Picard comparison. The infinitesimal calculation is imported, not re-planned here.

**Acceptance guards:**

- The Picard parameter is a sheaf of classes, not the automorphism groupoid of line bundles.

**Uses:**

- [StableReductionPartII:MC.7/picard-triples-comparison](#target-mc-7-picard-triples-comparison): For an algebraically closed field k in which N is invertible, geometric points of P_g,N^d identify with isomorphism classes of curve-level-line triples. For general bases retain the fppf sheafification and the obstruction/rigidification distinction; the existence of the parameter scheme does not produce a tautological line on every pulled-back curve.

**API:**

- `LevelPicardParameter.fiber` (characterisation): The fibre over a smooth curve-level point is its degree-d Picard scheme.
- `LevelPicardParameter.torsor` (structure): Picᵈ is a torsor under the relative Jacobian; there need not be a canonical origin.
- `LevelPicardParameter.obstruction` (compatibility): For p∈P^d(T) the Leray boundary δ(p)∈H²_fppf(T,G_m) vanishes exactly when an actual degree-d line bundle on C_T represents p, under O_T≅(f_T)_*O_{C_T} universally. The cohomological group is not identified with Azumaya classes without an additional theorem.
- `LevelPicardParameter.baseChange` (functoriality): Over any T→M_g[N], pullback of P_g,N^d represents the fppf degree-d Picard sheaf of C_T/T, with canonical identity/composition comparisons; no universal line is inferred.
- `LevelPicardParameter.tensor` (structure): Tensor product gives P^d×_{M_g[N]}P^e→P^{d+e}; O is the degree-zero unit and dualization P^d→P^{−d} gives the inverse. The degree-zero action on P^d is the stated Jacobian torsor action.
- `LevelPicardParameter.liftFiber` (characterisation): If δ(p)=0, tensoring any lift L by f_T*M identifies the set of line-bundle isomorphism classes lifting p with a Pic(T)-torsor. Two lifts differ by a unique base line-bundle class. For a field Pic(T)=0 this set is a singleton; general bases need not have that uniqueness.

**Unit tests:**

- `LevelPicardParameter.degreeZero` (computation): For d=0 the relative Picard component is the Jacobian with its canonical origin.
- `LevelPicardParameter.sectionRigidification` (compatibility): A chosen section permits rigidification and a Poincaré line; the unpointed universal family is not assumed to have that section.
- `LevelPicardParameter.scalarInertia` (non-example): The groupoid of triples has G_m scalar automorphisms of L; it cannot be identified with the represented Picard sheaf as a groupoid.
- `LevelPicardParameter.canonicalDegree` (computation): The dualizing line of the universal smooth curve determines a canonical section of P^{2g−2}; a canonical section of P¹ is not inferred from full level alone.
- `LevelPicardParameter.baseTwist` (non-example): Take T=P¹_C, a constant smooth genus-two curve C with fixed symplectic level3, and any degree-d line L on C. The lines pr_C*L and pr_C*L⊗pr_T*O(1) are distinct on C×T, as restriction along a C-point distinguishes them, but give the same point of the relative degree-d Picard sheaf. This rejects a parameter functor of unquotiented global line classes.
- `LevelPicardParameter.dualNumbers` (computation): For a fixed smooth genus-two curve over C with symplectic level3 and degree-d line L, first-order relative Picard deformations over C[ε]/(ε²) reducing to [L] form a torsor under H¹(C,O_C), a two-dimensional C-vector space. The constant lift chooses an origin. This rejects a functor keeping only reduced geometric points.

**Sources:**

- [yuan-author-http](#source-yuan-author-http), §4.3.2, printed/PDF pp.73–75; representability and geometric triples, pp.74–75. Defines the degree-d curve-level-line triples and the relative Picard parameter. The manuscript only needs the algebraically closed field comparison; general-base line lifting remains the specified Picard-owner input.
- [blr-relative-picard-LwkQQl](#source-blr-relative-picard-LwkQQl), §9.3 Theorem1 and proof p.252; §8.1 Leray discussion p.203 and Proposition4 pp.204–205. Representability/torsors apply on the Noetherian universal base. The exact obstruction sequence needs universal global functions; cohomological H²_fppf is not an asserted Azumaya identification.

<a id="target-mc-7-picard-triples-comparison"></a>
### Geometric triples and the Picard sheaf

**Target:** `StableReductionPartII:MC.7/picard-triples-comparison` (theorem).

For an algebraically closed field k in which N is invertible, geometric points of P_g,N^d identify with isomorphism classes of curve-level-line triples. For general bases retain the fppf sheafification and the obstruction/rigidification distinction; the existence of the parameter scheme does not produce a tautological line on every pulled-back curve.

**Hypotheses:**

- g≥2, N≥3 and d∈Z as in the parameter node; k is algebraically closed with N invertible, and the fixed pairing primitive root is part of the level datum. General-base remarks use the parameter node’s universal global-functions hypothesis.

**Dependencies:** [StableReductionPartII:MC.7/level-picard-parameter](#target-mc-7-level-picard-parameter), [StableReductionPartII:MC.4/level-rigidity](#target-mc-4-level-rigidity), `JacobianChallengePartII:JC4/actual-to-relative-obstruction`.

**Construction or proof route:**

1. Use the represented degree-d relative sheaf and JC4/actual-to-relative-obstruction. Over algebraically closed k a local fppf representative lifts to an actual line by choosing a k-point in a nonempty finite-type open of its covering scheme. Hence its Leray boundary vanishes. Pic(k)=0 makes the actual line class unique. This gives the bijection without reconstructing general Brauer cohomology theory here.
2. Use MC.4/level-rigidity to identify curve-level representatives uniquely up to their prescribed isomorphism; passage to line-bundle classes removes scalar inertia. For general bases, boundary vanishing only gives existence, and base Picard twists still give multiple actual line classes.

**Acceptance guards:**

- Scalar automorphisms disappear only after passage to classes.

**Sources:**

- [yuan-author-http](#source-yuan-author-http), §4.3.2, printed/PDF p.75, first two paragraphs. The stated bijection is explicitly for algebraically closed fields; the additional general-base obstruction distinction is an imported Picard-sheaf contract, not a assertion of a universal line bundle in this passage.

The 2026-10-05 MC.0/MC.1 audit confirms only stage contracts, not all supplier implementations: the accepted SF.1 nodes inspected concern set-valued algebraic spaces and Galois gerbs, not a geometric category-valued stable-curve stack. The generic DM §4 atlas and stack valuative criteria are stated without proofs. Exact geometric-fibre infinitesimal, unramified-to-quasi-finite, Noetherian source-dense valuative and strict-completion-to-étale criteria remain owner obligations. Native pullback comparisons, the fppf topology and proper-plus-locally-quasi-finite finiteness are now explicit pinned references.

For U_g construct the complete-canonical-polarization locally closed Hilbert locus and its projective-frame representing property, including the base-line twist; generic Hilbert representability and equal Hilbert polynomials do not by themselves prove this locus comparison. These owner extensions are mathematical input obligations, not compilation failures. The arbitrary-base Hodge bundle/determinant and forgetting/clutching comparisons also consume this extension; parent cohomology over locally Noetherian bases alone does not establish them for every scheme. The universal Isom source is specified as the projective-frame action groupoid U_g×PGL_r; proving that functor identification uses the actual canonical frame locus and must preserve its base-line twist. Its smooth-curve source density, not density only on U_g×U_g, feeds the refined Noetherian test. The named general criteria and descent interfaces must still be supplied.

R09.6 promises comparison of deformation functors with completed local rings and algebraization; its present stage description does not itself specify the coherent-sheaf Ext local-to-global spectral sequence, nodal differential resolution, H² vanishing or finite-support H¹ vanishing used here. Identify exact supplier nodes or an owner extension for that package and its source hypotheses. DM Lemma1.3/Proposition1.5 verifies this curve application, but naming generic formal deformation theory is not a proof of these inputs.

Knudsen 2012 pp.15–16 identify completion along the exceptional fibre with the completed polynomial Proj model before reflecting flatness. R09.6 states generic versality/algebraization, not compatibility of completion of relative Proj Sym K with completed cokernels and section quotients. Require this exact owner-level interface with local Noetherian and faithful flatness hypotheses, the old-mark collision comparison, and the existing arbitrary-base approximation input. The polynomial flat chart calculation alone is insufficient.

### G19 — Integral boundary normalization and deformation-line descent

Obtain precise owner contracts for finite relative node-choice/branch data in a nodal family and finite normalization of reduced DM stacks through étale atlases; SF.1/R09.5 generic descriptions and the parent finite-étale field theorem do not alone state them. For the conormal, prove the first-order smoothing line is the tensor of branch cotangent lines under arbitrary higher-order parameter changes, with unsigned branch-exchange and all atlas/graph/base-change cocycles over Z. Hacking 2008 pp.813–814 supplies the characteristic-zero normalization and conormal description; CLP v3 pp.4–5 supplies consumer graph-invariant usage, not the integral proof. Do not substitute Knudsen II Theorem 3.5 torsion differentials for the moduli conormal.

**Needed by:** [StableReductionPartII:MC.3/boundary-normalization](#target-mc-3-boundary-normalization), [StableReductionPartII:MC.3/clutching-finite-unramified](#target-mc-3-clutching-finite-unramified), [StableReductionPartII:MC.3/node-conormal](#target-mc-3-node-conormal).

### G20 — Integral parameter-family generation and fixed-line ampleness

The local logical route is repaired by the direct finite-degree-equations prerequisite. Its exact relative Serre generation/vanishing, fibre-ideal flatness, pluricanonical base-change and fixed-line openness interfaces still need verified SF.0/parent suppliers, as in the existing foundational gap. On one quasi-compact noetherian integral parameter family over Z, relative Serre generation and vanishing for the ideal sheaf of the relative tricanonical embedding give a common degree d. The ambient projective bundle and curve are flat, hence the ideal pulls back to each fibre ideal; the degree-d equations generate it. The multiplication quotient is surjective and the stable pluricanonical direct images have arbitrary-base-change comparisons. After applying the fixed-degree determinant criterion on every geometric fibre, fixed-line openness of relative ampleness spreads this one determinant over Spec Z. Preserve these qualifications; do not replace them by a maximum of varying fibrewise exponents.

**Needed by:** [StableReductionPartII:MC.4/projective-coarse](#target-mc-4-projective-coarse).

## Source findings

Findings are scoped to the identified copies and exact locators. Existing independent verdicts and source-version receipts remain in the packet; publisher-wide collation and novelty are separate obligations. Each description states the issue in our own words.

### StableReductionPartII/E1 — gap

**Source:** [knudsen2](#source-knudsen2), Main Lemma2.2 and its application,pp.175–178, published1983 scan.

**Issue:** The source labels the result as the main lemma.

**Corrected contract:** The pointed-node versality needed by the dual ideal calculation must be proved; use Knudsen2012 Proposition2.1 and §§2–4.

**Reason:** Knudsen2012 explicitly identifies the earlier unproved versality assumption and supplies the small-extension and matrix calculations.

### StableReductionPartII/E2 — error

**Source:** [knudsen2](#source-knudsen2), Proof of Theorem3.7,pp.187–189; Ile Remark6.4/Example6.5 PDF20–21.

**Issue:** JJ∨ = J

**Corrected contract:** Restrict the claimed nodal ideal relations to the nodal-section locus before the rank-two calculation.

**Reason:** For R=S[x,y]/(xy−bc) and I=(x−b,y−c), Ile computes R/(I I∨)≅S/(b,c) and I∨⊗S≅S⊕S/(b,c). The quotient is not rank2 on the whole smoothing base.

### StableReductionPartII/E3 — error

**Source:** [knudsen2](#source-knudsen2), Corollary3.9(b),printedp.190 (PDF30), published1983 scan.

**Issue:** The source asserts that β_{g₁,g₂,H,K} gives a closed immersion whenever g₁ ≠ g₂ or n ≠ 0.

**Corrected contract:** Use finite unramified clutching and boundary normalization by distinguished-node choices. A global separating clutching map need not be a closed immersion even for unequal genera and n>0.

**Reason:** Over C glue three pairwise nonisomorphic elliptic curves in a chain and put the sole mark on the central curve. The genus3 target has two distinct nodes of type (1,empty)|(2,{1}). Choosing the left or right elliptic tail gives nonisomorphic geometric preimages in M̄₁,₁×M̄₂,₂, since the first elliptic factors are nonisomorphic. A closed immersion is injective on geometric points. This is a statement counterexample, distinct from Ile’s correction to the proof of3.7.

### StableReductionPartII/E4 — gap

**Source:** [yuan-author-http](#source-yuan-author-http), §3.1.4,p.45,21August2024 author manuscript.

**Issue:** The source identifies a stable compactification with the closure of S′ inside M′g in the Zariski topology.

**Corrected contract:** Close the finite image in S̄₀×V and normalize in K(W₀), retaining both the base coordinate and the finite cover’s isomorphism data.

**Reason:** For a constant curve family on A¹, the image in V is zero-dimensional while a compactification of the base has dimension1. Moreover the stack fibre product remembers an isomorphism and can map finitely, not injectively, to S×V.

### StableReductionPartII/E5 — misprint

**Source:** [yuan-author-http](#source-yuan-author-http), §1.6,p.16,21August2024 author manuscript.

**Issue:** The source requires each rational irreducible component of C_k̄ to meet the other irreducible components in at least three points.

**Corrected contract:** Count the two normalization branches of every self-node; the three-intersection condition applies to nonsingular rational components.

**Reason:** A nodal rational component attached to an elliptic component has three normalization flags and is stable of total genus2 although it meets the other component only once. The parent and DM definitions count normalization flags.

### StableReductionPartII/E6 — error

**Source:** [clm](#source-clm), Introduction,p.1,1July2021 author manuscript.

**Issue:** The source describes the scheme over Z as projective, smooth and irreducible.

**Corrected contract:** Delete smooth for the coarse scheme; the stable stack is smooth.

**Reason:** Smoothness of an algebraic stack does not establish smoothness of its coarse quotient. The later NSF-deposited copy p.1 explicitly removes the word smooth.

### StableReductionPartII/E7 — error

**Source:** [clm](#source-clm), Lemma1.5 proof,p.4,1July2021 author manuscript.

**Issue:** The source asserts a subgroup inclusion of Pic(X) in Pic(U).

**Corrected contract:** Use the groupoid-equivariant descent datum and norm construction; forgetting equivariance need not be injective.

**Reason:** For Bμ_N over an algebraically closed field of characteristic prime to N, distinct character line bundles become the same trivial line on the atlas Spec k. The later NSF copy pp.4–6 replaces the argument by descent and norms.

### StableReductionPartII/E8 — gap

**Source:** [clm](#source-clm), Lemma7.1 proof,p.30 (lemma begins p.29),1July2021 author manuscript; NSF Lemma1.44 proof,PDF39.

**Issue:** The source deduces that S is Noetherian from its finite map to M_g.

**Corrected contract:** Require finite type/noetherian source explicitly before applying relative Serre vanishing.

**Reason:** The assumption is finite fibres of the classifying map; finite fibres alone do not imply a finite morphism or a noetherian source. The later NSF copy p.39 supplies finite type instead.

### StableReductionPartII/E9 — misprint

**Source:** [clm](#source-clm), Proposition6.3 proof,p.25,2021 author copy; same line in NSF copyPDF33.

**Issue:** The source invokes the identity b∗ωS′ ∼= ωS.

**Corrected contract:** For the contraction b:S→S′ use b_*ω_S^{⊗m}≅ω_{S′}^{⊗m}, hence the equality of relative pluricanonical direct images.

**Reason:** The rendered NSF line puts the star below b and its argument on S′, reversing the domain of pushforward. If read instead as pullback, the identity also misses the exceptional divisor: for a blowup ω_S≅b*ω_{S′}⊗O(E). The intended pluricanonical pushforward equality is valid, but requires its own argument.

### StableReductionPartII/E10 — misprint

**Source:** [clm](#source-clm), Lemma7.1 final proof line,p.30,2021 author copy; NSF Lemma1.44 proofPDF40.

**Issue:** The source asserts ampleness of f_*ω^{⊗3d}_{X/S}.

**Corrected contract:** The conclusion supplied by the ampleness lemma is det(f_*ω^{⊗3d}_{X/S}) ample.

**Reason:** The lemma statement concerns λ_{3d}=det f_*ω^{3d}, and Proposition5.5/NSF1.33 concludes ampleness of det Q. Its invocation does not by itself conclude ampleness of Q.

### StableReductionPartII/E11 — error

**Source:** [ile](#source-ile), arXiv1110.3909v3 §2.3,PDF5, paragraph defining the syzygy functor; same assertion in publisher indexed §2.3 HTML, DOI10.1016/j.jalgebra.2013.08.024. Direct publisher request403; publisher PDF not read..

**Issue:** The source asserts, for every n>0, the isomorphism Hom̲_A(Syz_A^n M,N) ≅ Ext_A^n(M,N).

**Corrected contract:** Without further hypotheses use the cokernel of Hom_A(P₀,N)→Hom_A(ΩM,N) from 0→ΩM→P₀→M→0, then dimension shift. Quotienting by every map through every coherent projective module is generally a larger quotient. Additional Ext vanishing against projectives can make the quotients agree; no unrestricted stable-category formula is used here.

**Reason:** Take A=ℤ, M=ℤ/2 and N=ℤ. The finite free resolution is 0→ℤ --2→ ℤ→ℤ/2→0, hence Ext¹_ℤ(ℤ/2,ℤ)=coker(2:ℤ→ℤ)=ℤ/2. Its first syzygy is 2ℤ≅ℤ, which is coherent projective. Every map from that syzygy to ℤ factors through the syzygy itself, so stable Hom is zero. The source defines the stable category of all coherent modules, without a stable-reflexivity restriction in this paragraph. This refutes the unqualified assertion, not the paper’s later restricted approximation theorems.

### StableReductionPartII/E12 — error

**Source:** [clm](#source-clm), 2021 author copy Corollary 6.6 proof p.25; later NSF author copy Corollary 1.39 proof p.33.

**Issue:** The source deduces R¹f_*(ω^m(−C_t))=0 from the degrees on the fibres.

**Corrected contract:** Use generic global generation and the invertible image I of f_*ω^m→C_t*ω^m. Write I=C_t*ω^m(−D) with D effective; nef quotient positivity gives deg I≥0, hence m deg(C_t*ω)≥0. No special-fibre vanishing is needed.

**Reason:** Blow up a smooth constant genus-g≥2 family at one point of a fibre and take the strict transform of the constant section through that point. The special fibre is C∪E with E≅P¹ a rational tail; the section meets E away from the node. On E, ω_f^m(−C_t) has degree −m−1, so H¹(E,O_E(−m−1)) has dimension m. The normalization exact sequence shows the special fibre has nonzero H¹, whereas the smooth generic fibre has zero H¹ for m≥2. Since the fibres have dimension one, cohomology/base change forces nonzero R¹f_* at this fibre. The family is nodal with smooth generic fibre, exactly the stated range. The corollary conclusion remains valid by the corrected image proof.

### StableReductionPartII/E13 — gap

**Source:** [clm](#source-clm), 2021 author copy Theorem 7.2 proof p.31; later NSF author copy Theorem 1.45 proof p.41.

**Issue:** The source claims ampleness of π*L_m whenever m=3d with d≥max(d_p).

**Corrected contract:** First choose one common d on the integral finite-type scheme cover using relative Serre generation and vanishing for the flat embedding ideal. This ensures the multiplication quotient and fibre-equation criterion in every characteristic. Apply the fixed-degree ampleness lemma on every geometric fibre, and then fixed-line openness for this one determinant. The packet now makes the finite-degree-equations prerequisite direct.

**Reason:** Stacks Lemma 30.21.4 (tag 0D2N) spreads one fixed invertible sheaf. For each d it gives U_(p,d), which may depend on d. A finite cover chosen using one set of exponents does not by itself remain an ampleness cover after replacing all exponents by their maximum. No common-neighbourhood or monotonicity result for these determinant lines is proved in the cited passage. This is a proof-input gap, not a counterexample to integral projectivity.

### StableReductionPartII/E14 — misprint

**Source:** [stacks-projective-picard-review](#source-stacks-projective-picard-review), Tag0BXJ, Lemma31.29.5, displayed Picard-group isomorphism and opening statement, public HTML read2026-10-05.

**Issue:** The source claims that projective n-space over a UFD has Picard group Z.

**Corrected contract:** Add n≥1. For n=0 and R a field k, projective zero-space is Spec(k), whose Picard group is zero; the displayed map from Z is not an isomorphism. The application here has n=r²−1≥24, so its Picard computation remains valid.

**Reason:** The statement does not restrict n. Definition27.13.2 and the single standard chart of Lemma27.13.3 give P⁰_k=Spec(k). Every invertible module over k is free of rank one. Thus every O(m) on P⁰_k is trivial. The cocycle proof needs an overlap, absent at n=0.
